title: Private IP and Public IP Addressing
description: Understand the difference between private and public IPs and how Azure assigns them to resources.

data.text: A private IP address is reachable only inside your VNet or on-premises network. A public IP address is reachable over the internet. Azure VMs, App Services, and other resources can have one or both.

data.title: Assign a Static Private IP to a NIC (Azure CLI)
data.content: Reserve a specific private IP for a network interface.
data.code: az network nic ip-config update   --name ipconfig1   --nic-name myNic   --resource-group myRG   --private-ip-address 10.0.1.10

data.title: Associate a Public IP with a Load Balancer
data.content: Create a static public IP and associate it with a load balancer frontend.
data.code:
az network public-ip create   --name myPublicIP   --resource-group myRG   --sku Standard   --allocation-method Static

az network lb frontend-ip create   --lb-name myLoadBalancer   --resource-group myRG   --name lb-frontend   --public-ip-address myPublicIP

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Private IPs stay inside your VNet.
Public IPs are needed for inbound internet traffic.
Use static IPs for anything that other services need to reach consistently.
data.takeaway: Plan your IP scheme before deploying resources. Changing IPs after the fact can cause downtime.
